title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. S is smooth over T. There is an exact sequence (37) 0 → E' →u E → E'' → 0 of O_S-modules, and E carries a stratification relative to T. P' is a torsor under E'. P = P' ×^{E'} E is its pushout to an E-torsor. σ is a stratification (an infinitesimal 'horizontality' structure) on P. From (P',σ) one gets a section φ of P^∞_{S/T}(E'')/vδ(E), where δ(E) are the horizontal jets of E and v maps jets of E to jets of E''.

Picard–Fuchs operators. A differential operator D: E'' → F is called a Picard–Fuchs operator if its linearisation u_D: P^∞(E'') → F kills vδ(E). In effect, D annihilates the images in E'' of horizontal sections of E, i.e. the 'periods'. Then μ_D(P',σ) := ū_D(φ) ∈ Γ(S,F).

This page names that section. In the image it is 'la section de Manin de F associée à l'op. de Picard-Fuchs D et aux données (P',σ)'. There is a universal Picard–Fuchs equation with values in the presheaf P^∞_{S/T}(E'')/u Sol(E'), which recovers the section φ. In modern language this is an abstract, sheaf-theoretic version of Manin's homomorphism ('theorem of the kernel'). For an abelian scheme, a K-point gives a torsor under an extension of D-modules (de Rham cohomology with the Gauss–Manin connection). Applying a Picard–Fuchs operator that kills the periods to its 'period' gives the inhomogeneous term: a section of F, linear in the point.

Second paragraph. Now E has only a connection relative to T instead of a stratification. Integrable connections on P = P' ×^{E'} E (compatible with ∇_E) correspond to maps d_{P'}: P' → E⊗Ω¹_{S/T} satisfying
- equivariance: d_{P'}(x'+ξ') = d_{P'}(x') + d⁰_E(u ξ'), and
- flatness: d¹_E ∘ d_{P'} = 0.
This is correct. An affine connection ∇_P with ∇_P(x+ξ) = ∇_P x + ∇_E ξ is determined by its restriction to the image of P', since every local section of P is x'+ξ. Flatness is the vanishing of d¹ on the 'curvature'.

The first-order variant of the Picard–Fuchs notion uses differential operators Δ: E⊗Ω¹ → F vanishing on d⁰_E(u(E')). One only needs them modulo operators of the form Δ'∘d¹_E, since these vanish on cocycles anyway. Locally d_{P'} gives a section of E⊗Ω¹ well defined modulo d⁰_E(u ξ'). So Δ produces a well-defined global section ν_Δ(P',d_{P'}) ∈ Γ(S,F).

On the next page:
- The universal F is P^∞(E⊗Ω¹)/Im P^∞(E').
- Composing D_0 = Δ∘d⁰_E: E → F gives an operator that vanishes on E' and descends to a Picard–Fuchs operator D: E'' → F. It kills horizontal sections because d⁰ does.
- The claim is ν_Δ = μ_D: the stratified/jet-theoretic Manin section reduces to the connection-level one. The margin note 'faire la vérification' shows this was not yet checked.
errors: E is said to carry only a connection relative to T, with 'intégrable' crossed out. Yet the condition d¹_E∘d_{P'} = 0, and the requirement that it be compatible with d_{P'}(x'+ξ') = d_{P'}(x') + d⁰_E(uξ'), need d¹_E∘d⁰_E∘u = 0. So integrability of ∇_E, at least on u(E'), is tacitly needed for 'connexions intégrables sur P' to make sense.
The equality (48) ν_Δ = μ_D is asserted but explicitly left unchecked ('faire la vérification', next page).

The relation between stratifications and connections used in the comparison (via (30)) implicitly needs characteristic 0, or divided-power/PD care in characteristic p. This is not stated on the page; the dossier also treats the Cartier operation, so this matters.

ideas.what: Picard–Fuchs operator relative to an extension 0→E'→E→E''→0 of stratified modules: a differential operator on E'' whose linearisation kills the images of horizontal jets of E. Plus a 'universal Picard–Fuchs equation' with values in P^∞(E'')/u Sol(E').
ideas.modern_name: Picard–Fuchs / annihilating differential operator of a D-module quotient; universal Manin-type map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin (1963); abstracted by Coleman (1990), Chai (1991), Buium (1990s), Bertrand–Pillay

ideas.what: 'Section de Manin' μ_D(P',σ) ∈ Γ(S,F) attached to a torsor P' under E' with horizontal structure on its pushout, and a Picard–Fuchs operator D.
ideas.modern_name: Manin map / Manin homomorphism (theorem of the kernel), inhomogeneous Picard–Fuchs term of a normal function
ideas.usually_credited_to: Yu. Manin 1963; Coleman 1990; Chai 1991; Buium; Bertrand

ideas.what: Integrable connections on the pushout torsor P'×^{E'}E correspond to affine maps d_{P'}: P'→E⊗Ω¹ with equivariance and closedness.
ideas.modern_name: Connections on torsors under vector bundles with connection / extensions of D-modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Katz, Deligne, Messing on universal vector extensions)

ideas.what: First-order version ν_Δ via operators Δ on E⊗Ω¹ killing d⁰(u(E')), taken modulo Δ'∘d¹, and the comparison ν_Δ = μ_D with D induced by Δ∘d⁰_E.
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of the Manin map from stratification (jet) data to connection (de Rham) data

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, around 1972, an abstract sheaf-theoretic 'section de Manin' attached to a torsor under a submodule of a stratified module and a Picard–Fuchs operator. This anticipates the later formalisations of Manin's map by Coleman (1990), Chai (1991) and Buium. It works relative to an arbitrary base T, with a universal target sheaf.
missed.quote: on l'appelera la section de Manin de F associée à l'op. de Picard-Fuchs D et aux données (P,σ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a coordinate-free, universal (jet-sheaf valued) Manin map. That could serve Manin-kernel and Mordell–Lang-over-function-fields work, and possibly char-p/crystalline variants, given that the dossier also treats the Cartier operation.

missed.claim: The comparison ν_Δ = μ_D, reducing the stratification version to the connection version, is left unverified. The 'universal Picard–Fuchs equation' with values in the presheaf P^∞(E'')/u Sol(E') is only sketched.
missed.quote: Équation de Pic.-Fuchs universelle : à valeurs dans le préfaisceau P^∞_{S/T}(E'')/u Sol(E')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A universal Manin map with values in jet-quotient sheaves is close to Buium's differential-algebraic jet-space approach. A worked-out version in arbitrary characteristic would be useful.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck explicitly naming and abstracting Manin's construction (the 'section de Manin') in a general torsor/stratification framework, with a universal target. This is a notable unpublished detail. However, the underlying idea is Manin's, and later abstractions exist (Coleman, Chai, Buium), so it is not a genuinely new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the image reads 'la section de Manin de F associée' (Manin underlined), not 'section de Gauss-Manin'.
Line 2: the data are probably '(P',σ)' as on the previous page.
Line 4: likely 'elle redonne la section φ susdite' rather than 'elle vérifiera la section y du dit'.
Paragraph 2: '(au lieu d'une stratification)' rather than '(en vue d'une stratification)'.
'loc.!' is a marginal insertion before 'une section de E⊗Ω¹_{S/T}'.
